hook: In October 2026, global ocean surface temperatures hit historic highs.

sections.voiceover: In October 2026, global ocean surface temperatures hit historic highs.
sections.visual_cue: Global satellite map displaying sea surface temperature anomalies across oceans.
b_roll: Satellite view of global ocean surface

sections.voiceover: The National Centers for Environmental Information reported ocean departures reached 1.14°C above the monthly average. Where did 75 percent of the ocean warm?
sections.visual_cue: Data graph showing 1.14°C temperature spike alongside latitude grid between 60°S and 60°N.
b_roll: Oceanographic research buoy floating in open ocean
Computer display with sea surface temperature readings

sections.voiceover: However, the National Centers for Environmental Information reports these record departures lasted five consecutive months.
sections.visual_cue: Timeline chart highlighting five consecutive monthly record markers.
b_roll: Waves crashing against oceanic monitoring station
Data telemetry screen tracking ocean temperatures

sections.voiceover: The National Centers for Environmental Information reports 75 percent of the global ocean warmed above average.
sections.visual_cue: Historical climate baseline trendline from 1850 to 2026 surging upward.
b_roll: Wide shot of global ocean horizon at sunset

sections.voiceover: NOAA records dating back to 1850 show no warmer ocean temperatures than those in 2026.
sections.visual_cue: Rotating global ocean globe showing warm anomalies fade into historical archive emblem.
b_roll: Global satellite projection of Earth oceans
